title: blue-hill-payments-integration-call-notes-2026-03-28
content:
Call: Blue Hill Payments (BHP) integration kickoff - 2026-03-28 11:00 PT
Attendees: Ryan O'Neal (BHP - Eng), Mei Tan (BHP - Security), James Wu (BHP - Prod), Ava Martinez (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood Infra), Nora Davis (Redwood AM)

High-level ask:
- BHP wants to embed Redwood for fraud-scoring + policy assistant in their merchant onboarding flow.
- Hard requirement: must be deployable into their PCI-compliant VPC (no egress except to approved endpoints).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 220ms for single-turn scoring calls at expected peak concurrency (200 rps).
- Data residency: production must run in us-east-1 only; staging can be in us-west-2.

Notes / Context:
- BHP currently sends webhook payloads to a Node service that enriches transactions and calls into an internal rules engine. They want to replace/enhance parts with model outputs (scoring, suspicious-flag reasons, suggestion text).
- They prefer a deterministic, predictable cost model (Reserved/Dedicated pricing preferred) but want a POC on hosted API first.
- Security team flagged: no PII or PAN can be logged by third-party; keys must be managed via their KMS and no plaintext logs leaving VPC.
- Mei asked about KMS/HSM integration and ability to rotate keys under their control - Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS was presented as option.
- They use Postgres + Redis; plan to store embeddings for merchant profiles (embedding size TBD). Concerned about vector store in shared infra due to compliance.

Key technical requirements (from call):
- Private deployment (VPC) with egress controls + customer-managed KMS
- Model variants: need a fast, small model for scoring (low latency) and a larger model for human-readable explanations (can be async)
- API surface: single scoring endpoint that returns score, reason tokens, and optional follow-up text. Support for streaming not required initially.
- Auth: OAuth2 client creds + mTLS on the ingress path
- Observability: per-route latency + token counts + per-inference cost metrics surfaced to BHP; ability to export traces to their Datadog account
- Failover: synchronous fallback to lightweight rules engine if model service unavailable; Redwood routing policy capability demonstrated as match (can do model fallback).

Gotchas / Risks flagged in call:
- Tokenization: their rule engine expects short reason strings (< 250 chars). Longer explanations may break downstream pipeline. Need guideline on #tokens -> approximate chars for chosen models.
- Throughput target (200 rps) + low latency implies Dedicated capacity or heavy autoscaling on Private infra - MVP on hosted may not meet 95p latency at peak.
- Embedding storage in-host vs customer-managed vector DB: compliance likely mandates customer-managed DB inside VPC. We need clear docs/proof of concept for using Redis/PG vector store (or partner like Pinecone self-hosted).
- Billing: BHP procurement prefers fixed monthly commit. Need to route to Sales for Dedicated contract estimates.

Immediate action items (owners + target dates):
- Ava: Draft POC plan (hosted API minimal integration) and run baseline latency estimates with synthetic traffic modeled on BHP shape - due 2026-04-02.
- Liam: Validate Private deployment network diagrams + KMS integration approach; provide checklist of blocked egress ports and required endpoints - due 2026-04-04.
- Nora: Intro email + calendar invite to Sales (for Dedicated pricing) and Security SME from Redwood for deeper KMS discussion - by 2026-03-30.
- Sofia (internal): Create Jira epic BHP-128 and link to CONF-4212, include acceptance criteria and POC success metrics (95p latency target, max allowed cost per inference) - due 2026-04-01.

POC suggestion (internal recommendation):
1) Quick hosted POC: integrate with hosted API using masking on PII, sample payloads, and demo scoring endpoint. Goal: validate API shape and end-to-end latency in non-peak.
2) Private POC parallel: small Private deployment (1 node) in us-east-1 using customer subnets + customer-managed KMS, test end-to-end latency with BHP synthetic traffic and per-route tracing.
3) If Private proves latency and security, propose Dedicated reserved capacity contract for production.

Open questions to clarify with BHP:
- Exact payload sizes and average token counts for inputs they plan to send (need sample data).
- Do they require synchronous explanations for every score, or only for flagged items? (This impacts model selection & perf)
- Procurement timeline: when do they expect to sign a commercial agreement? (Sales needs to know for resource planning)
- Vector DB: do they have a required vendor? Are they open to hostable/self-managed options?

Useful links / refs from call:
- Confluence: CONF-4212 (PCI / Private deployment pattern)
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/solutions/pull/342 (vpc-private-deploy-docs)
- Jira: BHP-128 (placeholder created by Sofia)
- Slack thread: slack://channel/CMPLY789/project-blue-hill

Next steps (short term):
- Send follow-up email to BHP with proposed POC plan + ask for sample payloads (Ava, today)
- Kick off internal sync (Ava + Liam + Nora + Sofia) to draft POC runbook and required infra changes (this week)
- Sales intro + schedule demo for procurement/stakeholders (Nora to schedule)

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider offering a hybrid: keep scoring model lightweight on Private infra and offload explanation generation to a queued async hosted service (reduces peak capacity need).
- Prepare example token -> char mapping table for the models we propose (use gpt-style approximations) to give BHP quick guidance.
- Add internal checklist item: confirm we can disable request/response logging for tenant in Private deploy (Mei asked this explicitly).

Status: follow-up email drafted; awaiting sample payloads from BHP and internal confirmation on KMS approach.
